bib.title: Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain Question Answering
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 16th Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (EACL), pages 874-880

question: How much can a generative seq2seq reader benefit from retrieving text passages for open-domain QA, and does it scale with the number of passages?
hypothesis: Generative models can aggregate evidence from many retrieved passages better than extractive readers, so accuracy should keep improving as passages increase.
contributions: Fusion-in-Decoder: encode each question-passage pair independently, fuse in the decoder
State-of-the-art on NaturalQuestions and TriviaQA open benchmarks
Accuracy keeps improving up to 100 passages

method.summary: A retriever (BM25 or DPR) returns 100 passages; each is concatenated with the question and title and encoded independently by a T5 encoder; the decoder cross-attends over the concatenated encoder outputs and generates the answer. Models are fine-tuned per dataset.

datasets.name: TriviaQA (unfiltered)
datasets.split: as Lee et al. (2019); open-domain test and hidden test
datasets.preprocessing: uppercase answers converted with Python title()

datasets.name: SQuAD v1.1
datasets.split: validation used as test; 10% of training set kept for validation

datasets.name: Wikipedia dumps
datasets.source: Dec. 20, 2018 for NQ and TriviaQA; Dec. 21, 2016 for SQuAD
datasets.preprocessing: as Chen et al. 2017 and Karpukhin et al. 2020: passages of 100 words, non-overlapping

models.name: Fusion-in-Decoder (base)
models.context: each passage truncated to 250 word pieces

models.name: Fusion-in-Decoder (large)
models.context: each passage truncated to 250 word pieces

models.name: BM25
models.architecture: Apache Lucene, default parameters, SpaCy tokenisation

models.name: DPR
models.architecture: two BERT networks, dot product, FAISS approximate nearest neighbours

training.objective: inferred: sequence-to-sequence cross-entropy on the answer (not stated); target sampled from answer list for NQ and SQuAD, unique human answer for TriviaQA
training.compute: 425 GPU hours for NQ training on 100 passages (Section 4)

other.checkpoint_selection: evaluated every 500 steps, best on validation Exact Match
other.finetune_experiment: models trained with fewer passages then finetuned with 100 passages for 1000 steps (147 GPU hours)

inference.samples: single run per setting; no seeds or variance reported
inference.prompting: encoder input marked with special tokens question:, title:, context: before question, title and text of each passage
inference.retrieval: 100 passages unless stated; DPR for NQ and TriviaQA, BM25 for SQuAD

metrics.name: Exact Match
metrics.definition: correct if matches any acceptable answer after lowercasing and removing articles, punctuation and duplicated whitespace

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: SQuAD token F1 (not defined in the paper)

eval.protocol: Single runs; no significance tests; Table 1 on test sets, Fig 3 and Table 2 on validation/dev sets.

evidence.quote: constant learning rate of 10−4 and a dropout rate of 10%

results.claim: FiD-large reaches 51.4 EM on the NaturalQuestions test set, above RAG at 44.5.
results.setup: Fusion-in-Decoder (large) on NQ, TriviaQA and SQuAD Open test sets; 100 passages, DPR for NQ/TriviaQA, BM25 for SQuAD, T5-large 770M, greedy decoding
results.table: Table 1, row Fusion-in-Decoder (large), column NQ EM (RAG row: 44.5)

results.claim: FiD-large reaches 67.6 EM on TriviaQA open-domain test and 80.1 on the hidden test set.
results.setup: Fusion-in-Decoder (large) on NQ, TriviaQA and SQuAD Open test sets; 100 passages, DPR for NQ/TriviaQA, BM25 for SQuAD, T5-large 770M, greedy decoding
results.note: RAG: 56.1 open test, 68.0 hidden test. Hidden test is 80.1 for FiD-large.
results.table: Table 1, row Fusion-in-Decoder (large), columns TriviaQA EM (67.6, 80.1)

results.claim: FiD-base reaches 48.2 EM on NQ and 65.0 on TriviaQA open test.
results.table: Table 1, row Fusion-in-Decoder (base), columns NQ EM, TriviaQA EM

results.claim: FiD-large scores 56.7 EM on SQuAD Open, narrowly above Path Retriever (56.5 EM).
results.setup: SQuAD v1.1 open, BM25 retrieval, 100 passages
results.note: F1: FiD-large 63.2, below Path Retriever 63.8. FiD-base 53.4 EM / 60.6 F1 is below both Path Retriever and Multi-Passage BERT on F1.
results.table: Table 1, row Fusion-in-Decoder (large), columns SQuAD Open EM, F1

results.claim: Going from 10 to 100 retrieved passages improves TriviaQA by 6% and NQ by 3.5% (FiD-base, valid sets, same k in training and test).
results.setup: FiD-base, validation sets, Fig 3; values per k only as plot
results.where: Section 4, Scaling with number of passages
results.quote: increasing the number of passages from 10 to 100 leads to 6% improvement on TriviaQA and 3.5% improvement on NaturalQuestions

results.claim: Training with fewer passages lowers accuracy when testing with 100 passages: NQ w/o finetuning 37.8 at 5 passages vs 46.5 at 100.
results.setup: FiD-base, test with 100 passages, dev sets
results.table: Table 2, rows 5 and 100, column NaturalQuestions w/o finetuning

results.claim: Finetuning with 100 passages for 1000 steps closes most of the gap: 46.0 EM on NQ at 147 GPU hours versus 425 GPU hours for training on 100 passages throughout.
results.setup: NQ dev, models first trained with 25 or 50 passages (Table 2 w/ finetuning shows 46.0)
results.where: Section 4, Impact of the number of training passages
results.quote: we can reach 46.0 EM on NaturalQuestions, using 147 GPU hours, compared to 425 GPU hours when training on 100 passages

results.claim: Table 2 w/ finetuning TriviaQA: 5 training passages 64.2, 10 passages 63.6, 25 passages 64.2, 50 passages 64.3; w/o finetuning 100 passages 64.7.
results.table: Table 2, column TriviaQA w/ finetuning (64.2, 63.6, 64.2, 64.3) and w/o finetuning row 100 (64.7)

results.claim: Retrieval beats parameters: FiD with 770M parameters plus Wikipedia/BM25 scores 44.1 on NQ versus closed-book T5 11B at 36.6.
results.note: 44.1 appears only in the text, not in Table 1; Table 1 has FiD-large at 51.4 on NQ (the retriever used for Table 1 is DPR per Technical details). So 44.1 is presumably the BM25 variant, which the paper never tabulates.
results.quote: while our approach obtains 44.1% with 770M parameters plus Wikipedia with BM25 retrieval

results.claim: Encoding passages independently makes compute grow linearly, not quadratically, in the number of passages.
results.quote: the computation time of the model grows linearly with the number of passages, instead of quadratically

results.claim: Extractive models peak at 10 to 20 passages (cited, not run by the authors).
results.source: Wang et al., 2019; Yang et al., 2019
results.quote: the performance of most extractive models seems to peak around 10 to 20 passages

limits: Paper has no limitations section; conclusion says efficiency at large passage counts is future work
Retrieval is not trained jointly with the reader
No timing measurements: linear-cost claim is architectural
Passage order and position effects not tested
Only short-answer QA; single runs, no variance
Text reports 44.1 NQ with BM25 which is not in Table 1

terms.definition: passages are processed independently in the encoder but jointly in the decoder; the model performs evidence fusion in the decoder only

differs in how passages are processed
